definitions.explanation: The circular orbit high above the equator in which a satellite's orbital period matches the Earth's rotation, so it appears to stay fixed over one point on the ground.

examples.japanese: ⟦{衛星|えいせい}→衛星：01880_eisei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{静止軌道|せいしきどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{置|お}く→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: To place a satellite in geostationary orbit.

examples.japanese: {静止軌道|せいしきどう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{衛星|えいせい}→衛星：01880_eisei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{地上|ちじょう}→地上：12108_chijou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{止|と}まって→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: A satellite in geostationary orbit appears stationary from the ground.

examples.japanese: ⟦{通信|つうしん}→通信：03514_tsuushin⟧⟦{衛星|えいせい}→衛星：01880_eisei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{多|おお}く⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{静止軌道|せいしきどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{配置|はいち}→配置：14409_haichi⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Many communication satellites are placed in geostationary orbit.

notes:
USAGE: {静止軌道|せいしきどう} is the geostationary orbit, in which a satellite circles the Earth once per day and so appears to hover over a fixed point. It is widely used for communication and weather satellites.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {静止軌道|せいしきどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}せる→乗せる：01972_noseru⟧: to put into geostationary orbit
- {静止軌道|せいしきどう}⟦{衛星|えいせい}→衛星：01880_eisei⟧: a geostationary satellite

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{円軌道|えんきどう}→円軌道：29617_enkidou⟧: circular orbit
- ⟦{楕円軌道|だえんきどう}→楕円軌道：29618_daenkidou⟧: elliptical orbit
